propositions: acli_graph.py hand-rolls the same nextPageToken cursor loop three times with no runaway-token guards, allowing a server that repeats the same token to spin infinitely (cabc bug class).

When a server returns an identical non-null nextPageToken consecutively, the loop must raise RunawayPaginationError and escape the fail-open exception handler, preventing silent partial-dict degradation.

The three pagination readers in acli_graph must consolidate into a single shared cursor iterator that drives POST body's nextPageToken, terminates on isLast:true or absent token, and guards against token repetition.
Ordinary transport exceptions caught by the fail-open handler must still degrade gracefully to partial results; only RunawayPaginationError must propagate and interrupt the map.
Offset-protocol pagers (fetcher._iter_pages, jira_datacenter/transport.py::_paged_search) remain untouched and independently tested to mitigate consolidation regression risk.
